village.text: Nestled in the Rabodeau valley, Grandrupt is a Vosges village full of character, where fir forests meet green meadows. With fewer than a hundred inhabitants, it offers an authentic way of life, far from the bustle of the city, while providing its residents with essential services.

presentation.title: Grandrupt, in the heart of the Vosges
presentation.p1: Nestled in the Rabodeau valley, between fir forests and green meadows, Grandrupt is a Vosges village full of character. With just under a hundred inhabitants, it offers an authentic and peaceful way of life in the heart of the Vosges mountains, a few kilometres from Senones.
presentation.p2: The village covers about 9 km² at an average altitude of 400 metres. Its landscapes, typical of the Hautes-Vosges, its state forests and its streams make Grandrupt a place to recharge, popular with nature lovers and hikers.

history.title: A few pages of history
history.p1: The earliest written records of Grandrupt date back to the Middle Ages, when the village appears in the registers of Senones Abbey. Like many Vosges hamlets, it grew up around forestry and woodworking, activities that long shaped the local economy and landscape.
history.p2: Over the centuries, Grandrupt has lived through the great chapters of Lorraine's history: wars, annexations, reconstruction. Successive generations have preserved the identity and solidarity typical of Vosges villages, passing on a shared heritage of simplicity and resilience.
history.p3: Today, the municipality continues to provide its residents with essential services while preserving its exceptional natural setting. The town hall remains the heart of community life, keeping residents connected and local traditions alive.
